rules.sentence: Generally, diagnosis is similar to that of other dementias (. Clinical criteria (including a thorough history and standard neurologic examination) are 85% accurate in establishing the diagnosis and differentiating Alzheimer's disease from other forms of dementia, such as vascular dementia and Lewy body dementia.
However, deviations from these criteria do not exclude a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, particularly because patients may have mixed dementia.
Distinguishing Alzheimer's disease from other dementias is difficult.
Assessment tools (eg, Hachinski Ischemic Score—see) can help distinguish vascular dementia from Alzheimer's disease.
Fluctuations in cognition, parkinsonian symptoms, well-formed visual hallucinations, and relative preservation of short-term memory suggest Lewy body dementia rather than Alzheimer's disease (see).
